Subject: Re: LIVE - streaming responses stalling intermittently (started ~20:40 PT) — initial findings

War room notes (first-pass):
- Reproduced under high-concurrency replay: we see a backlog at the proxy-to-runtime connection where chunk frames stop being forwarded for periods consistent with customer report (6–13s).
- Error mode: proxy returns 502 on some client reconnects; when stream resumes, token output is resumed mid-response (no truncation).
- Root cause hypothesis: a regression in continuous-batching prefetch introduced in 2028-05-10 that interacts poorly with HTTP connection pooling under bursty usage. The runtime is not dropping requests, but the proxy buffer appears backpressured and stalls emitting chunked frames.

Immediate actions taken (in prod shadow/fallbacks):
1) Rolled traffic for Novacorp to fallback pool with conservative batching and increased worker counts.
2) Toggled keepalive to 6s at edge and added a heartbeat token (0x01) emitted every 4s for long-running streams.
3) Disabled the prefetch optimization for affected model family to validate hypothesis.

Preliminary result: error rate dropped by ~60% over 20 minutes and throughput recovered ~18% on the fallback pool. We still see rare 6–8s stalls while connections drain.

Next: capture a targeted trace around proxy->runtime buffer metrics, collect GC and thread dumps for the runtime process during repro. I’m attaching a short diagnostic PNG that shows buffer depth over time.

Rishi
Lead SRE, Serving Runtime
